title: Some overlap here with my Spring roundup, but several additions made ...
transcript: the Broadway season might technically be over but the New York Theatre season is still very much in full swing! here's a bunch of shows opening in may that I think should be on your radar so this isn't even including summer openings which I'm gonna make a separate video about soon but opening in may alone we have another show from the director who did the Sarah Snook Dorian Gray and the Cynthia Erivo Dracula this one isn't a solo show though it's a revival of the Maids by Jean Genet starring Yerin Ha from Bridgerton we have the return engagement of Well, I'll Let You Go which a lot of people are buzzing about right now this is a beautifully crafted play about grief that has some of the best actors in New New York we got the revival of Animal Wisdom by the genius composer/storyteller Heather Christian I'm so pumped for this one! the Emporium is fascinating it's technically a world premiere of a previously unproduced, unfinished play by one of the most famous playwrights of the 20th century, Thornton Wilder it's been adapted and completed, I guess, by the playwright Kirk Lynn and apparently there's like an audience voting component to the production? we got this musical adaptation of the film a Girl Interrupted with a score by Aimee Mann and it stars King Princess and speaking of Princess we have Indian Princesses a new play about a father daughter program for girls of color with white fathers. and speaking of programs for young girls we have Girls Chance Music about a gifted music program this one's written by Eisa Davis who some of you might know as the co writer of Warriors with Lin-Manuel Miranda but of course she's a very accomplished artist in her own right Clubbed Thumb’s SummerWorks series is one of my favorite annual traditions and I'll talk more about it in my summer round up but the first show of the series is happening in May Titans is described as: “the ordinary residents of an overrun American city” “answer the signal and discover their extraordinary powers.” “unfortunately they must be brave.” Jerome is a new play by John J Caswell Jr who broke onto the scene in a big way a few years ago with two very weird plays Wet Brain and Scene Partners and this one is about an older gay couple in rural Arizona we got the return engagement of a Woman Among Women which is a really tender thoughtfully conceived play inspired by Arthur Miller's All My Sons And Then the Rodeo Burned Down is the next show from the kookie clown duo Xhloe and Natasha, who are on a real hot streak right now I very much enjoyed both the shows I've seen from them so far and I've heard great things about this one too. Have You Ever Thought About is closing pretty soon I posted about this one yesterday it's a whimsical, highly interactive performance art theatre experience that kind of feels like elementary school thought exercises for adults. and all the shows I just mentioned begin performances in may or at the very end of April But there's also some productions that started in April but are closing in may like Bedlam's 4-person version of Othello which I just saw yesterday and it was like maybe the most well acted production of Othello I've ever seen also closing soon is production of Hamlet starring Hiran Abeysekera who you might remember from Life of Pi on Broadway a few years ago and a show I've raved about many times already: Rheology a performance art piece that he performs with his real life mother and it's about anticipatory grief and the physics of sand
classificationReason: Creator lists multiple shows opening in May (The Maids, Well I'll Let You Go, Animal Wisdom, The Emporium, and more) with no single production as the primary focus. Classic preview/roundup format.
